# S3-Compatible Object Storage: Solution Landscape

## On-Cluster Open-Source Solutions

### MinIO

MinIO was the dominant self-hosted S3-compatible object store until its progressive closure between 2021 and 2026. Timeline:

| Date | Event | Citation |
|------|-------|----------|
| October 2019 | Apache 2.0 components began migrating to AGPL | [32] |
| May 2021 | License transition to GNU AGPLv3 completed (RELEASE.2021-05-11T23-27-41Z) | [32] |
| May 2025 | Web console / management UI stripped from community edition | [33] |
| October 15, 2025 | Last community release published | [2] |
| December 3, 2025 | Repository placed in maintenance mode | [1] |
| April 25, 2026 | Repository archived (read-only) | [5] |

The commercial successor, MinIO AIStor, starts at approximately $96K/year for 400TB [2][35]. Support tiers include Enterprise (4-hour P1 response, 24/7, unlimited Panic Button) and Enterprise Lite (5-business-day response) [14].

**Forks:** The pgsty/minio fork has accumulated approximately 1,375 stars and packages the last known-good source with CVE patches, though it carries single-maintainer risk [5][90]. The OpenMaxIO community fork stalled shortly after creation [34]. "No fork of MinIO community edition has gained traction" [1].

MinIO held a Red Hat certified container stack listing in the ecosystem catalog [22].

### Ceph / Rook

Rook is a CNCF graduated project [53] that provides a Kubernetes operator (Apache 2.0 licensed [53]) for Ceph (dual-licensed LGPL 2.1 or LGPL 3.0 [52]). Ceph's RADOS Gateway (RGW) component exposes the S3 API.

Red Hat Ceph Storage, the enterprise-supported distribution, is now available exclusively with Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift [37]. Standalone Red Hat Ceph Storage is no longer offered as an independent product.

Premium partner support for upstream Rook is available through Clyso GmbH for managed services, consulting, and emergency support [36].

### SeaweedFS

SeaweedFS is an Apache 2.0-licensed object store [54] with approximately 31,000 GitHub stars, under active development since 2012 [3]. The latest release is v4.21 (April 2026) [5].

The architecture uses a Master+Volume+Filer topology [29]: masters handle metadata and topology, volume servers store data, and filers provide a POSIX-like namespace. High availability requires 3 masters forming a RAFT consensus group [3].

SeaweedFS has been adopted by Kubeflow Pipelines as an S3-compatible backend [5].

### Garage

Garage is an AGPL-3.0-licensed object store [30] with approximately 3,600 GitHub stars, developed by the Deuxfleurs French non-profit association [2]. The latest release is v2.3.0 (April 2026) [5].

The architecture is based on the Amazon Dynamo paper, using CRDTs for consistency across geo-distributed nodes [2]. Garage is designed for multi-site deployments with built-in geo-redundancy [3].

Limitations: no erasure coding and no Object Lock support [5].

### RustFS

RustFS is an Apache 2.0-licensed object store [31] with approximately 26,000 GitHub stars, currently at v1.0.0-alpha.99 [5]. The project was accepted into the NVIDIA Inception Program in April 2026 [82] and claims 2.3x performance over MinIO for 4KB payloads [82].

Security concerns are significant: 13 security advisories were filed between December 2025 and April 2026, including a critical XSS vulnerability [5]. The project explicitly states "Do NOT use in production" [2].

An OpenShift operator exists with multi-tenant namespace support and cert-manager integration [6].

### Versity S3 Gateway

Versity S3 Gateway is an Apache 2.0-licensed project with approximately 2,256 GitHub stars, at v1.4.1 [5]. It acts as an S3 facade over a POSIX filesystem rather than implementing its own storage engine. Object Lock support is partial [5].

## On-Cluster Commercial Solutions

| Solution | Deployment Model | OpenShift Integration | Key Detail | Citation |
|----------|-----------------|----------------------|------------|----------|
| Scality ARTESCA | Kubernetes-native | Ships with MetalK8s; COSI/CSI drivers open-source (Apache 2.0) | HPE partnership, entry <$4K/year for 50TB | [42][43][67] |
| Dell ObjectScale | Kubernetes-native | Software Bundle or Application on customer-managed OpenShift | Kubernetes-native evolution of ECS | [48][68] |
| Portworx | Operator-based | Red Hat certified operator via OperatorHub | Abstraction layer for S3 backends (AWS, FlashBlade) since v2.12 | [20][21] |
| VAST Data | CSI driver | Red Hat certified CSI operator | External system, not on-cluster; S3 via multi-protocol | [66][49] |
| Cloudian HyperStore | Appliance/software | OpenShift support announced; RHEL OpenStack certified | Military-grade security (Common Criteria, FIPS) | [64][83] |

### Scality ARTESCA

ARTESCA is Kubernetes-native with dual-layer erasure coding [42]. Deployment options include Software Appliance, Hardware Appliance, ARTESCA+Veeam All-in-One (10-120TB), and Pay-as-You-Go [41]. Entry-level pricing starts under $4,000/year for 50TB usable with 24x7 support included, scaling to 8.5PB [43]. ARTESCA includes a $100K cyber guarantee [41].

The COSI and CSI drivers were released as open-source under Apache 2.0 [67].

### Dell ObjectScale

ObjectScale is available as a Software Bundle or as an Application deployed on customer-managed Red Hat OpenShift [68][48]. It represents Dell's Kubernetes-native evolution from the ECS platform.

### Portworx

Portworx holds Red Hat certified operator status [21] and is available through OperatorHub [20]. It provides an abstraction layer that can front S3-compatible backends including AWS S3 and Pure Storage FlashBlade since version 2.12 [20]. Portworx advertises zero-RPO disaster recovery and sub-60-second pod recovery [20].

### VAST Data

VAST Data provides a Red Hat certified CSI operator [66] for OpenShift. The storage system itself is external (not on-cluster), exposing S3 alongside NFS and SMB via multi-protocol access [49]. S3 features include object versioning, object lock (added in v4.3), multipart uploads, and IAM [49].

### Cloudian HyperStore

Cloudian announced OpenShift support [64] and holds RHEL OpenStack certification [83]. The platform emphasizes compliance certifications including Common Criteria, FIPS, and NIST 800-88 [83].

### Wasabi Pricing Traps

Wasabi's headline $6.99/TB rate carries two constraints that significantly affect small or short-lived workloads. A 1TB monthly minimum means storing 100GB effectively costs $0.069/GB — 10x the headline rate [40][79]. A 90-day minimum storage duration means deleting data before 90 days still incurs charges for the full 90-day period [39]. For data retained fewer than 23 days, AWS S3 is cheaper [79].

### Cloudflare R2

R2's zero-egress model eliminates the cost barrier that 55% of IT leaders cite as the biggest switching impediment in cloud storage [80][8]. However, the S3 feature set is substantially limited — no versioning, ACLs, policies, tagging, object lock, SSE-KMS, replication, website hosting, or event notifications [7].

## Structural Observations

Foundation-hosted projects (CNCF, Apache Software Foundation, Linux Foundation) are "immune to these rug-pulls" that affected MinIO [1]. The MinIO trajectory — Apache 2.0 to AGPL to feature-stripping to archival — illustrates the risk of single-vendor open-source projects, particularly those backed by investors pressuring for relicensing [56].

AGPL licensing (MinIO, Garage) is a "non-starter for most companies" due to corporate bans (Google completely prohibits AGPL [55]), M&A friction, and the network-use clause that closes the SaaS loophole [75].

## Gaps and Limitations

1. **Pricing opacity** — Scality ARTESCA, Dell ObjectScale, Cloudian HyperStore, and VAST Data do not publish per-TB pricing. The ARTESCA entry-level figure (<$4K/year for 50TB [43]) is from a 2023 press release and may not reflect current pricing.
2. **Azure and GCS details sparse** — No primary-source S3 compatibility documentation was collected for Azure Blob Storage or Google Cloud Storage interoperability APIs.
3. **Cloudian depth** — The OpenShift support announcement [64] lacked deployment architecture details. The RHEL OpenStack certification [83] is from 2016 and may not reflect current integration status.
4. **VAST Data on-cluster ambiguity** — VAST is listed as off-cluster with a CSI driver, but whether VAST software can run on OpenShift worker nodes (vs. requiring dedicated appliances) was not confirmed.
5. **RustFS production readiness** — GitHub star count (~26K) significantly exceeds the project's maturity. The alpha designation and 13 security advisories in five months warrant caution despite rapid community growth [5][31].
